- Which subprocessors (compute, storage, CDN, monitoring) may have access to data or logs during normal operation?
- If we create a deletion request for customer data and request logs removed, what are the SLA timelines and what gets deleted vs retained for compliance (audit logs, billing records)?

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I’m happy to firm any item up for contract language or hop on a call. I’ve also attached our regional processing matrix (pdf) for detail.

Short answers (hosted API):
- Regions: Primary inference clusters are in US West (us-west-2) and EU West (eu-west-1). We also have optional endpoints in US East (us-east-1) for latency-sensitive customers; region selection is policy-driven and can be constrained per-customer with a routing rule.
- Subprocessors: compute/storage - AWS (EC2/EBS, S3), GCP (optional for EU capacity), CDN - Fastly/CloudFront for streaming / web assets, monitoring/logs - Datadog, error reporting - Sentry, identity/KMS - AWS KMS / customer-managed KMS for Private/Dedicated.
- Cross-border: By default, requests are routed to the nearest compatible region by latency and capacity. If residency is required, customers can pin to a region or choose Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments to avoid cross-border routing entirely.
- Retention & deletion: For hosted API, temporary request payloads and model context are kept in memory and KV caches; ephemeral logs (debug traces) are retained 30 days by default; aggregated telemetry and billing records are kept for billing/compliance for up to 7 years (encrypted). Deletion requests for customer-specific artifacts (request logs, cached prefixes) are processed within 30 days; audit/billing records required by law are retained as stated above. Dedicated/Private options allow configurable retention windows and can disable marketplace telemetry.

Next steps: I can send a short statement of work language that you can drop into the appendix, or we can schedule a 25-min call. Marcus, Aditya — please add anything critical I missed for the hosted flow.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Laura / Aditya — additions to the bullets before we finalize copy for procurement: 

- Inference routing details: the serving runtime uses smart routing (latency/cost policy). That means a given request may touch a regional routing layer in us-west-2 or eu-west-1 depending on model variant and available GPU capacity. For strict residency customers we need to either: 1) pin the customer to a single region via routing policy, or 2) use Dedicated capacity which guarantees no cross-region fallbacks.
- Caching: KV cache is per-instance and ephemeral; prefix caching can persist across requests for the customer within the same region. We can include a clause that prefix cache is considered transient application data and will be cleared on deletion request within the 30-day SLA.
- Subprocessor nuance: we use GCP in eu-west for some EU-only capacity (GCE + regional storage) and have a contractual DPA with Fastly for content delivery and with Datadog for observability. Where customers require, we can provide a list of subprocessor locations and subprocessors' SOC2 attestations.
- Deletion evidence: we can provide an attestation letter and a short runbook that shows the deletion job, confirm the deletion window, and provide a minimal audit trail proving the request was executed (timestamps, operator id).

Suggestion: propose Redwood Dedicated for the procurement appendix as an option — it simplifies the residency guarantee and shortens the deletion SLA to 14 days for cached artifacts (we currently commit 30 days for hosted).

-Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Operations
